## Proposal: January 15 H-1B Intake Deadline

For the upcoming cap season, I propose that we set January 15 as our internal deadline for H-1B registration intake. We would send engagement letters and a one-page questionnaire during the week of December 7, then handle anything received after January 15 case by case. The goal is better service: a clear timeline for employers and enough room for us to review information carefully before registration opens.

Last March, we filed 14 registrations for six employer clients. Nine of those 14 matters came in during the final week of February, and Rosa logged roughly 11 hours of overtime during the week the registration window opened. That crunch was largely a function of our process, not client delay: we currently send the questionnaire whenever an employer asks, without giving them a target date. One HR contact told me she would have happily sent everything in January if we had asked.

An earlier deadline also gives us time to catch problems. Last season, Brightwater Analytics sent a beneficiary’s passport scan two days before the window opened. It had expired in October, and we caught it because Rosa checked the dates. Registration itself is simple, but errors can be expensive: an incorrect passport can mean an invalid selection. January 15 is realistic—HR teams are back from the holidays, budgets are set, and employers already plan for the $215-per-beneficiary registration fee in Q1.

**What would change:**

- Send engagement letters and the one-page questionnaire the week of December 7.
- Ask employers to complete intake by January 15; review later requests case by case.
- Have Rosa own the tracker, with a clean six weeks to chase missing information and resolve gaps before the expected registration window.

Marcus and I can settle on the approach Thursday so we are ready to send the December letters.
